fills.researcher_notes: SAME company-level question decided once for the whole brief (P1124/P2299/P2300) — see P1124's shard for the full sourcing writeup. This row's current Operator, 'Turkmengaz, Uztransgaz, Intergas Central Asia', is a CORRECTION target, not just a gap-fill: three independent sources (Order of the Minister of Energy №350 §44 [adilet.zan.kz], cdu.ru, qsamruk.kz) all name ТОО «Азиатский газопровод» / Asia Gas Pipeline LLP (AGP) — a 50/50 QazaqGaz/KazTransGas + CNPC-subsidiary JV formed 2008-02-15 specifically to build/operate the Kazakh Section — as operator of the Kazakhstan-China trunk system, all three strings. 'Intergas Central Asia' does not appear as operator of this pipeline in any source found; it is instead documented (intergas.kz) as operator of the older Soviet-era systems (Central Asia-Center, Bukhara-Urals, Okarem-Beyneu) via its regional Main Gas Pipeline Departments (UMG) in Atyrau, Aktau, Uralsk, Aktobe, Kostanay, Shymkent and Taraz — a different corridor with a different corporate operator, likely a sheet mix-up between two distinct KazTransGas-family entities. Turkmengaz and Uztransgaz are retained (Turkmen- and Uzbek-section operators, consistent across every source including the wiki) but were not independently re-verified this session; only the Kazakh-section entity was the open question here.

validity.recommendation: Owner: retain the multi-entity union (this row already carries PipeChina; Turkmengaz; Uztransgaz; QazaqGaz) — genuine shared ownership across the corridor's national sections, applies identically to Lines A/B/C, not a duplication artifact. But 'PipeChina' is a naming concern: P1124 (Line C) reads 'China National Petroleum Corp' for the same slot, and I could not verify which name is current. Per china.aiddata.org, AGP's Chinese-side 50% shareholder is 'Trans-Asia Gas Pipeline Company Limited' (a CNPC subsidiary as of the 2008-2015 period; reportedly restructured via a 2015 CNIC Corp Ltd stake sale and a later merger into 'Sino-Pipeline International Company Limited', per web search I could not verify against a primary corporate filing this session). PipeChina (National Oil and Gas Pipe Network Group Co Ltd, est. 2019) is China's DOMESTIC pipeline consolidator; no source found shows it absorbed CNPC's overseas JVs like AGP, so 'PipeChina' here looks more likely to be the imprecise label of the two. Recommend a human pick one Chinese-side name and apply it to all three rows uniformly rather than editing this alone without a primary corporate-registry source.
